answer: A work-backed reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks: every agent identity earns trust only through verified tasks attested by independent peers, growing slowly like rings of a cedar, easy to audit and hard to fake. New identities start isolated like an island, with strict rate limits and no credit, so an attacker must pay real compute and time for each fake. A copper-bottomed stake is slashed on misbehavior, making one trusted identity cost more to forge than a hundred empty ones earn.
